title: Fix tf.linalg.det gradient crash on singular matrices

labels.name: python
labels.description: Pull requests that update Python code

body:
## Problem

Computing the gradient of `tf.linalg.det` via `tf.GradientTape` crashes with `InvalidArgumentError: Input is not invertible` when the input matrix is singular (`det(A) = 0`). The same issue affects `tf.linalg.slogdet`. Reported in issue #119477.

```python
m = tf.constant([[1.0, 2.0], [2.0, 4.0]], dtype=tf.float64)
with tf.GradientTape() as tape:
    tape.watch(m)
    d = tf.linalg.det(m)
g = tape.gradient(d, m)  # InvalidArgumentError: Input is not invertible
```

## Root cause

`_MatrixDeterminantGrad` implements `grad * det(A) * A^{-H}` by calling `matrix_inverse`, which raises for singular matrices. The same issue exists in `_LogMatrixDeterminantGrad`.

## Fix

- **`_MatrixDeterminantGrad`**: compute `det(A) * A^{-H}` directly from the SVD `A = U @ diag(s) @ V^H` as

  ```
  det(A) * A^{-H} = det(U) * conj(det(V)) * U @ diag(prod_except) @ V^H
  ```

  where `prod_except[i]` is the product of all singular values except `s[i]`, built from exclusive left/right cumulative products (no division by zero). This agrees with the previous formula for invertible inputs, extends continuously to singular ones (for real `A` it is the transpose of the classical adjugate), and handles complex dtypes correctly via `conj(det(V))` and `adjoint_b=True`. Batched inputs are supported.

- **`_LogMatrixDeterminantGrad`**: use the SVD-based pseudoinverse in place of `matrix_inverse` so the backward pass stays finite for singular inputs (where `log|det(A)| = -inf` and the gradient value is inherently undefined).

## Tests

New `DetGradSingularMatrixTest` in `linalg_grad_test.py`, running in both graph and eager modes:

- singular 2x2 checked against the closed-form adjugate
- invertible 2x2 checked against the closed-form adjugate
- batch mixing singular and invertible matrices
- complex128 matrix checked against `det(A) * A^{-H}`
- slogdet on a singular matrix: gradient finite, no exception

The SVD formula was additionally cross-validated numerically against closed-form cofactor adjugates for singular, rank-1, zero, random, and complex matrices.

Fixes #119477.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44559

📝 Summary of Changes
This PR is the first in a series of four.

PR 1/4: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44559   <--- This PR
PR 2/4: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44560
PR 3/4: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44562
PR 4/4: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44564

These PRs aim to enable the Triton backend for the All-Gather collective operation based on the experimental tiling strategy.

title: Fix RangeOp abort on extreme float ranges before allocation

labels.name: comp:core
labels.description: issues related to core part of tensorflow

body:
Fixes #122746

### Description

Calling `tf.range` with extreme floating-point scalars can make `RangeOp`
infer a very large output length that still fits in `int64`. The existing
overflow guard therefore does not reject it, and the kernel attempts a
multi-terabyte allocation. Under AddressSanitizer this aborts the process
(`allocation-size-too-big`) instead of raising a recoverable TensorFlow
error.

Example from the issue (float64):

- inferred length ≈ `2_619_754_293_846` elements
- requested bytes ≈ `20.96 TB`

### Solution

Reject Range outputs whose byte size is at least `1 TiB` before
`allocate_output`, returning `InvalidArgument`. Mirror the same check in:

- Range shape inference (`math_ops.cc`) so graph mode fails consistently
- `RaggedRangeOp` for the same allocation class

### Changes

- `tensorflow/core/kernels/sequence_ops.cc` — pre-allocation byte-size check
- `tensorflow/core/ops/math_ops.cc` — matching shape-inference check
- `tensorflow/core/kernels/ragged_range_op.cc` — matching values-size check
- C++ tests: `sequence_ops_test.cc`, `ragged_range_op_test.cc`
- Python test: `math_ops_test.py` (`RangeTest.testExcessiveFloatAllocation`,
  graph and eager)

### Tests

- `//tensorflow/core/kernels:sequence_ops_test`
- `//tensorflow/core/kernels:ragged_range_op_test`
- `//tensorflow/python/ops:math_ops_test`

title: PR #45332: [ROCm] Fall back to library collective for non-uniform replica groups
body:
PR #45332: [ROCm] Fall back to library collective for non-uniform replica groups

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45332

The collective (one-shot/two-shot) AllReduce kernel bakes the clique size (world_size) as a compile-time constant from the first replica group and sizes its signal/staging buffers the same way. With non-uniform replica groups (e.g. axis_index_groups=[[0,1],[2,3,4,5,6,7]]) the single emitted kernel runs on cliques of different sizes, causing out-of-bounds peer accesses (GPU page fault) and hangs on gfx950.

Reject the collective kernel when replica groups differ in size so the op falls back to the library (RCCL/NCCL) collective, which handles heterogeneous cliques. Uniform replica groups are unaffected.

## 📝 Summary of Changes
Add a uniformity guard to `IsAllReduceKernelSupported` (`xla/backends/gpu/runtime/all_reduce.cc`): if any replica group's size differs from the first group's size, the custom collective AllReduce kernel is not selected and the op falls back to the library (RCCL/NCCL) collective. No device-code changes; uniform replica groups continue to use the kernel unchanged.

## 🎯 Justification
The collective kernel's clique size (`world_size`) is a codegen-time constant taken from the first replica group, and its signal/staging buffers are sized the same way. A single AllReduce with non-uniform replica groups therefore emits one kernel that is then run across cliques of *different* sizes, which reads/writes past the per-rank buffers → GPU page fault (`SQC` client, addr `0x0`) and/or a wedged HSA queue and hang. This is observed on ROCm/gfx950 with e.g. `pmap` + `axis_index_groups=[[0,1],[2,3,4,5,6,7]]`. Any workload that issues an AllReduce over uneven replica groups is affected; the kernel is architecturally single-clique-size, so falling back to the library collective (which handles heterogeneous cliques) is the correct behavior.

## 🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix

## 📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
N/A — this is a correctness fix. It only diverts non-uniform-group AllReduces (which are broken today) to the library collective; uniform-group AllReduces still use the custom kernel, so no performance change for supported cases.

## 🧪 Unit Tests:
No new unit test in this commit. A targeted addition would be an assertion that `IsAllReduceKernelSupported(...)` returns an `Unimplemented` status for a replica-group set with differing group sizes (e.g. `{{0,1},{2,3,4,5}}`) and remains supported for uniform groups — happy to add this if desired.

## 🧪 Execution Tests:
Covered by the existing `tests/pmap_test.py::PythonPmapTest::testPsumUnevenReplicaGroups`, which exercises uneven `axis_index_groups` and previously hung. Note this cannot be expressed within the "at most 2 GPUs" guidance: non-uniform replica groups require at least 3 devices (two groups of different sizes), and the test itself skips when `device_count <= 2`. Validated on 8x MI355X (gfx950) with the kernel enabled: full ROCm UT suite passes — single-accelerator `29118 passed` (1 pre-existing unrelated DLPack waiver), multi-accelerator `854 passed, 0 failed` (previously wedged at this test). Path confirmed via VLOG: uneven groups → 0 kernel launches / all RCCL; even groups → kernel used.

title: PR #45070: [ROCm] [xla:gpu]VMM command-buffer: skip-remap + copy-into-shadow for launch-bound regimes
body:
PR #45070: [ROCm] [xla:gpu]VMM command-buffer: skip-remap + copy-into-shadow for launch-bound regimes

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45070

## Summary
This one followed by #44726 as optimization:

Optimize the ROCm VMM command-buffer VA-remapping path (`ExecuteWithVaRemapping`) so that trace-once capture + replay (`NEVER_UPDATE`) is a net win in launch-bound (tensor-parallel) regimes, where the per-step VA remap previously outweighed the benefit.

The optimization is based on two properties of the per-step remap on ROCm:

- Most command-buffer slots (model weights) keep the same backing physical buffer across steps, yet the existing path unmapped and re-mapped the entire reservation every step — and on ROCm `hipMemUnmap` is the dominant per-step cost.
- A small number of tiny slices (scale/scalar/metric buffers) change address every step and are the worst case for remapping (a full unmap/map/SetAccess round-trip costs milliseconds even for a few bytes).

Two ROCm-gated changes; the CUDA path and the default ROCm behavior are unchanged:

1. **Skip-remap** — cache each slot's source (BFC) address and only remap the slots whose backing buffer actually moved, reusing the in-tree, unit-tested `se::MemoryReservation::ScopedMapping::Remap()`. In steady state (nothing moved) it issues zero driver calls and skips the unmap-event sync. Default ON for ROCm; set `--xla_gpu_command_buffer_vmm_skip_remap=false` to force the legacy path for A/B.
2. **Copy-into-shadow** — keep tiny churning slices out of the contiguous reservation and give each a stable shadow buffer (fixed address baked into the replayed command buffer), refreshed each step with a stream-ordered D2D copy instead of a remap. Opt-in via `--xla_gpu_command_buffer_vmm_copy_threshold_bytes` (bytes; `0` = default, disabled).

Both knobs are standard XLA flags (`xla.proto` / `DebugOptions`), not environment variables; they are read from the module's `DebugOptions` and only take effect on ROCm.

## Performance

Measured with MaxText (synthetic data, identical converged loss across configurations). Numbers are **relative per-step speedups** (steady-state median, after warm-up), **normalized to the default baseline configuration**; absolute throughput is omitted. Each model compares the default baseline config against the VMM-optimized config (trace-once replay + collectives captured + per-step remap minimized). Baseline = `1.00×`; higher is faster.

### 8×MI300X

| model       | baseline (default) | VMM-optimized |
| ----------- | :----------------: | :-----------: |
| llama2-7b   | 1.00×              | 1.09×         |
| llama3-8b   | 1.00×              | 1.16×         |
| llama3.1-8b | 1.00×              | 1.17×         |
| mistral-7b  | 1.00×              | 1.14×         |
| gemma2-9b   | 1.00×              | 1.23×         |
| qwen3-8b    | 1.00×              | 1.13×         |

### 8×MI355

| model       | baseline (default) | VMM-optimized |
| ----------- | :----------------: | :-----------: |
| llama2-7b   | 1.00×              | 1.10×         |
| llama3-8b   | 1.00×              | 1.16×         |

A consistent end-to-end per-step improvement across popular dense LLMs on both platforms, largest on the most launch-bound models. In the bandwidth-bound FSDP regime the same configuration is performance-neutral (no regression).

a407b1298a594be9eb887afbd6f0868c4b8415fc by Pham Binh <phambinh@amd.com>:

[xla:gpu][ROCm] Skip remapping unchanged command-buffer VA slots

The VA-remapping command-buffer path (ExecuteWithVaRemapping) unmapped the
entire reserved VA range and re-mapped every command-buffer allocation on
every step, even though most slots (model weights) keep the same backing
physical buffer step-to-step. On ROCm the VA unmap is the dominant per-step
cost, so this full remap is wasteful.

Wire the already-in-tree, unit-tested se::MemoryReservation::ScopedMapping::
Remap() per-slice skip primitive into the per-step path: cache each slot's
source (BFC) address from the previous step and mark remap_required only for
slots whose backing buffer moved. Unchanged slots keep their mapping (no
unmap/map/SetAccess), and when nothing changed the unmap-event sync is skipped
entirely (steady state issues zero driver calls).

ROCm-gated (VmmRemapSkipEnabled); the CUDA path keeps its existing
reset()+MapTo behavior. XLA_VMM_SKIP_REMAP=0 forces the legacy path for A/B.

Measured (8xMI300X, FSDP=8, 8 layers, NEVER_UPDATE, 30 steps), median ms/step:
  llama2-7b: 1096.5 -> 552.0  (1.99x)
  llama3-8b: 1284.0 -> 616.0  (2.08x)
Identical converged loss; no crash.

ffecfda0301f1ccd7a2db64f60ae2373bcd14bec by Pham Binh <phambinh@amd.com>:

[xla:gpu][ROCm] Copy-into-shadow for small command-buffer VA slots

Small command-buffer slices (tiny scale/scalar/metric buffers that churn
their address every step) are the worst case for VMM per-step remapping: a
full hipMemUnmap/hipMemMap/hipMemSetAccess round-trip costs ~2-4ms even for a
few bytes, and there can be many such slices per step.

This change keeps those slices OUT of the contiguous VA reservation and instead
gives each a stable shadow device buffer (allocated once, fixed address baked
into the replayed command buffer). Each step the shadow is refreshed with a
stream-ordered D2D copy (real->shadow before execute, shadow->real after) rather
than a remap. Gated by XLA_VMM_TMP_COPY_THRESHOLD (bytes; 0 = disabled, default),
ROCm-only, so the CUDA path and default ROCm behavior are unchanged.

Combined with the per-slot skip-remap, this makes capturing collectives into the
command buffer (NEVER_UPDATE) a net win in launch-bound (tensor-parallel) regimes.
Loss/correctness unchanged.

[xla:gpu][ROCm] Address second review round on copy-into-shadow

- Fail loudly when a copy-into-shadow slice grows after first capture: under

b3a577e0c51ce8aaf07130941ac4d2c7aa0d28c0 by Pham Binh <phambinh@amd.com>:

[xla:gpu][ROCm] Address round-2 review on VMM skip-remap + copy-into-shadow

Fixes from the second claude-review pass on PR #1001:

- Skip-remap: if ScopedMapping::Remap() fails, reset scoped_mapping before
  returning the error. Remap() consumes the mapping via std::move, so leaving
  the (now moved-from) optional with has_value()==true would make the next
  step's skip path call Remap() on an empty mapping (UB). Resetting forces the
  legacy reset()+MapTo() recovery path instead.
- VaRanges destructor: synchronize unmap_event before deallocating the shadow
  buffers. The last step's command buffer may still be using them on the
  device, and hipFree on in-use memory is UB on ROCm. Marked
  ABSL_NO_THREAD_SAFETY_ANALYSIS (runs at teardown, no other thread present).
- Add ABSL_GUARDED_BY(mutex) to the mutex-protected VaRanges fields
  (va_reservation, unmap_event, scoped_mapping, last_mapped_src_addrs,
  small_shadow) so the thread-safety analyzer enforces the locking.
- Debug-only DCHECK that the per-slot reservation offsets are stable across
  steps, making the skip-remap "same allocation per slot" invariant explicit
  (new last_mapped_offsets companion vector, populated only in non-NDEBUG).
- ParseVmmRemapSkipEnabled: treat empty XLA_VMM_SKIP_REMAP the same as unset
  (default ON), matching ParseVmmCopyThresholdBytes; add a unit test.

[xla:gpu][ROCm] Address review: experimental flags + split ExecuteWithVaRemapping

Rename the two VMM command-buffer knobs with the xla_gpu_experimental_ prefix
(xla_gpu_experimental_command_buffer_vmm_skip_remap and
xla_gpu_experimental_command_buffer_vmm_copy_threshold_bytes); they are meant to

279ab0076a19ce2e1846105c1f83cb8434fe134d by Pham Binh <phambinh@amd.com>:

[xla:gpu][ROCm] Always maintain last_mapped_offsets (drop #ifndef NDEBUG)

The per-slot reservation-offset bookkeeping used by the skip-remap DCHECK was
guarded by #ifndef NDEBUG to keep the release hot path free of the work. Measured
in isolation (-O2 -DNDEBUG) the maintenance is ~10-150 ns per step at typical
command-buffer slot counts (tens to hundreds), <=0.3 us at 512 slots, and N*8
bytes of RAM -- negligible next to the microsecond-to-millisecond
hipMemUnmap/hipMemMap it sits beside. Drop the preprocessor guard and always
populate it for readability; the DCHECK is still compiled out in release.

63638b5ac1835becd46d85af4498a8935f58df5a by Pham Binh <phambinh@amd.com>:

[xla:gpu][ROCm] Temporarily disable collective command-buffer capture under VMM to fix numerical correctness

Under the VMM VA-remapping command-buffer update modes (NEVER_UPDATE /
CAPTURE_CMD_NEVER_UPDATE) a collective is traced into the command buffer once
and then replayed. On ROCm the traced RCCL collective binds its buffers at
trace time and does not follow the per-step physical remap / copy-into-shadow
refresh; additionally, on multi-GPU its cross-rank data-ready synchronization
is not re-established on HIP-graph replay (replay re-runs only the GPU kernel,
not RCCL's host-side proxy work-counter progression). The replayed collective
therefore reads stale buffers and silently corrupts results whenever the
collective's buffers churn across steps (e.g. TP/FSDP training; observed as
space_TP=8 loss divergence).

As a temporary correctness fix, do not convert collectives to command buffers
on ROCm in these VMM update modes -- run them eagerly instead. All
non-collective ops (fusions, gemms, custom-calls) remain captured. This trades
the collective-capture performance benefit for correctness until RCCL supports
graph-replay-safe collectives (fully kernel-driven intra-node collectives, or
replay-safe symmetric / user-buffer registration).

ALWAYS_UPDATE re-records the collective each step and is unaffected.
NVIDIA/CUDA behaviour is unchanged (ROCm-gated).

Fix xla.proto field-number collision surfaced by the merge

The textual auto-merge of xla/xla.proto left the PR's two ROCm VMM flags at
DebugOptions field numbers 505/506, which upstream's main-mirror history had
meanwhile assigned to xla_gpu_cudnn_deviceless_compilation_mode (505) and
xla_gpu_enable_nccl_user_buffers_in_default_space (506). protoc rejected the
duplicate field numbers. Renumber the PR flags to the next free numbers:

b4aebe0c2a49b2bbc1af985a6031b7c0e4bfd909 by Pham Binh <phambinh@amd.com>:

Resolve merge: port PR VMM allocator to upstream persistent-index API

The origin/main-mirror merge conflicts in gpu_executable_buffer_allocator.
{cc,h} were overlapping rewrites: the PR's ROCm-safe VMM command-buffer
allocator (whole-range VA reservation + skip-remap + copy-into-shadow) vs
~163 upstream commits that refactored the allocator around a new
`persistent_alloc_indices` command-buffer mechanism and a ThunkExecutor*
constructor.

Resolution keeps the PR's ROCm-safe VA-remap/copy-shadow implementation
byte-for-byte (upstream's per-allocation partial-range hipMemSetAccess path
crashes on ROCm) and adapts it to upstream's interface:
- Add CommandBufferAllocationIndexes { persistent, va_remapped }; collect both
  in CollectCommandBufferAllocationIndexes (constants -> persistent only;
  non-constant command allocs -> both).
- Constructor takes ThunkExecutor* and collects the index sets internally.
- ExecuteWithBufferAllocations / ExecuteWithVaRemapping thread
  persistent_alloc_indices through the execute callback so the command-buffer
  thunk traces once and skips per-step updates for stable (reserved-VA/shadow)
  addresses; GetPersistentAllocIndices() returns nullopt when the scope is not
  driving VMM remapping (legacy behavior).
- All VA-remap internals (EnsureVaReservation, ComputeReservationOffsets,
  BuildStepMappingPlan, CreateExecutionScope) now iterate the va_remapped set.

Pure-VMM correctness preserved: 1-GPU VMM command-buffer replay loss matches
eager base exactly across all steps (max |delta| = 0.000). Compiles clean.
The temporary-disable-collective fix (command_buffer_conversion_pass.cc) is
untouched. ROCm-gated only; no CUDA/BFC changes.

Merging this change closes #45070

title: [XLA:CPU] Evaluate allocation requirements dynamically during parameter bufferization in XTile.
body:
[XLA:CPU] Evaluate allocation requirements dynamically during parameter bufferization in XTile.

In upstream XTile parameter bufferization (`xtile_bufferization.cc`), `ExtractTileOp` and `InsertTileOp` unconditionally generate runtime boundary checks (`scf.if`) and local scratch buffer allocations (`memref.alloc` / `memref.copy`) whenever a tile is not statically proven to be full size.

This CL optimizes parameter bufferization by evaluating allocation and boundary check requirements dynamically during the bufferization pass:
* Implements live analysis (`ShouldAllocateForLayoutFixup`, `IsAlwaysFullSize`, and `IsPerfectTiling`) in `xtile_ops.cc` to inspect layout, vector ABI alignment (`mlir::DataLayout`), contiguous slices, and perfect divisibility.
* When `IsPerfectTiling` is true (buffer dimensions perfectly match tile sizes and strides) and there is no vector alignment or layout mismatch, bufferization safely elides both the runtime boundary check (`scf.if`) and scratch buffer allocation (`memref.alloc`), wrapping the subview directly in `to_tensor`.
* Adds `DataLayoutInterfaces` dependency to support target-specific vector alignment queries during bufferization.

### Comparison to Option B (`cl/917192693`) & Architectural Rationale

We evaluated two distinct approaches to eliding unnecessary scratch allocations:
* **Option A (This CL - Live Bufferization Analysis)**: Evaluates allocation requirements dynamically during the bufferization pass by inspecting the target IR, layouts, and vector alignment directly at the point of bufferization.
* **Option B (`cl/917192693`, http://cl/917192693 - Cached Lowering Attribute)**: Evaluates allocation requirements earlier during HLO lowering and attaches a boolean `should_allocate` attribute to `ExtractTileOp` and `InsertTileOp`.

We selected Option A (Live Analysis) over Option B for the following reasons:
1. **Compiler Robustness & IR Decoupling**: Keeps HLO lowering clean and decoupled from bufferization optimization metadata. Evaluating requirements live during bufferization ensures the optimization remains robust across intermediate MLIR transformations (such as CSE or canonicalization) that might modify IR without updating cached attributes.
2. **Safety & Vector Alignment Correctness**: Option B stamped `{should_allocate = false}` at lowering time based solely on `IsPerfectTiling`, unconditionally bypassing layout fixup checks during bufferization. This could unsafely elide scratch buffers when target DLTI vector ABI rules require specific memory alignment. Option A checks layout, contiguous slices, and vector ABI alignment first, ensuring correct fallback allocation when required by alignment or layout constraints.
3. **Performance Parity & Compilation Speed Improvements**: A 10-run PerfLab A/B benchmark sweep on `arcadia-rome` (32 cores vs. `cl/917192693`, http://sponge2/aa143681-a8af-42e0-aa36-2f8b8f4a3e52) confirmed that runtime execution performance (`time/op`) is statistically indistinguishable (-0.11% geomean delta across 39 benchmarks). Meanwhile, compilation speed (`BM_CompileHloModule`) improves by up to ~5% on dot-heavy models under Option A by eliminating attribute bookkeeping and reducing IR bloat during lowering.

title: [XLA:GPU] Propagate tiling through single-user bitcasts/transposes/reshapes when checking slice fusion worthiness.
body:
[XLA:GPU] Propagate tiling through single-user bitcasts/transposes/reshapes when checking slice fusion worthiness.

When determining if a slice is worth fusing, traverse through single-user bitcasts, transposes, and reshapes from the slice's operand. This allows the check for multiple users to be applied to the instruction before these single-user operations, enabling more opportunities for fusion.

title: Fix STABLEHLO case and scatter tests with delegate support
body:
Fix STABLEHLO case and scatter tests with delegate support

- StablehloCaseTest: Pass input tensor type to Build*Subgraph in
  StablehloCaseStaticOpModel and StablehloCaseDynamicOpModel.
  During delegate application (`interpreter->ModifyGraphWithDelegate`),
  any delegate (e.g. YNNPACK, XNNPACK, GPU) queries `IsNodeSupportedByDelegate`
  against all subgraph nodes. Because subgraphs previously defaulted to int32
  tensors, delegates supporting int32 claimed the ops. During `AllocateTensors()`,
  `STABLEHLO_CASE::Prepare()` updated subgraph input types to int16, forcing the
  delegate's `Prepare()` to process int16 tensors which it never inspected or
  accepted during delegate selection.

- StablehloScatter: Use `pre_delegation_execution_plan()` in `GetComputationType()`.
  Higher-order ops (like `stablehlo.scatter`) inspect their body subgraph during
  `Prepare()` to identify the reduction operation. When any delegate claims a
  body subgraph op, TFLite replaces that op in `execution_plan()` with a
  delegate node, causing `STABLEHLO_SCATTER::Prepare()` to fail. Using
  `pre_delegation_execution_plan()` allows `stablehlo.scatter` to inspect the
  original operation regardless of which delegate claimed the body op.

title: [XLA:Service] Fix ASan stack-use-after-scope in HLO verifiers and tests
body:
[XLA:Service] Fix ASan stack-use-after-scope in HLO verifiers and tests

When verifier classes (e.g., `ShapeVerifier`, `InstructionVerifier`) are instantiated directly with inline temporary `HloVerifierOpts{}` rvalues in standalone tests or utilities, storing options by const reference (`const HloVerifierOpts& opts_`) causes a dangling reference hazard. When the temporary expression terminates, the options object is destroyed on the stack, resulting in an AddressSanitizer (ASan) `stack-use-after-scope` abort upon dereferencing member fields like `opts_.layout_sensitive`.

This change fixes the lifetime vulnerability by:
1. Updating `ShapeVerifier` and `InstructionVerifier` to safely manage `HloVerifierOpts` lifetimes rather than retaining vulnerable const references to temporary options.
2. Updating `hlo_verifier_test.cc` to bind `HloVerifierOpts` to local lvalue variables before passing them to `ShapeVerifier`, ensuring the options outlive the verifier instance during test execution.

title: PR #45345: [GPU] Prepare DSF V2 embedded thunks with fusion-local buffer allocations
body:
PR #45345: [GPU] Prepare DSF V2 embedded thunks with fusion-local buffer allocations

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45345

📝 Summary of Changes
Thunks inside DSFv2 fusion use slices numbered against a allocation list, which is internal to fusion. Unlike ExecuteOnStrem/Record, the Prepare phase passes the module level indexing instead of building the internal buffer allocation. As a consequence FFI custom calls with Prepare callback will be indexed against the wrong allocation list.

🎯 Justification
FFI customer calls with Prepare callback will crash when module level allocation is smaller, and silently wrong when larger.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)
N/A.

🧪 Unit Tests:
Behavior scope is too large for a unit test to catch. N/A.

🧪 Execution Tests:
Added.
Copybara import of the project:

--
efbd4995ae25343cd91acb48d8d7e9278c30d0a5 by Terry Sun <tesun@nvidia.com>:

[xla:gpu] Prepare DSF V2 embedded thunks with fusion-local buffer allocations

DynamicSliceFusionV2Thunk::Prepare forwarded the module BufferAllocations to
embedded thunks whose slices are relative to the fusion-local
embedded_allocations_. Embedded thunks that resolve buffers at prepare time
(FFI custom calls with a prepare-stage callback) read unrelated allocations:
the extent check in BufferAllocations::GetDeviceAddress fails when the
same-indexed module allocation happens to be smaller, and silently produces
addresses into unrelated buffers otherwise. Build the same fusion-local view
that ExecuteOnStream and Record already build; without live loop state,
loop-dependent offsets resolve to their clamped initial values.

Adds a regression test where the DSF hero is an FFI custom call with a
prepare-stage handler that must observe the same fusion-local result buffer
as the first execution.

Merging this change closes #45345

title: tf.histogram_fixed_width with infinite value_range can trigger ASan SEGV in HistogramFixedWidthFunctor
body:
### Issue type

Bug

### Have you reproduced the bug with TensorFlow Nightly?

Yes

### Source

source

### TensorFlow version

tf.version.VERSION: 2.21.0-dev0+selfbuilt

### Custom code

Yes

### OS platform and distribution

Linux Ubuntu 22.04

### Mobile device

_No response_

### Python version

Python 3.10.12

### Bazel version

bazel-9.1.0

### GCC/compiler version

gcc (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.2) 11.4.0

### CUDA/cuDNN version

_No response_

### GPU model and memory

_No response_

### Current behavior?

Calling `tf.histogram_fixed_width` with `values` containing `+inf` / `-inf` and `value_range=[-inf, inf]` can crash the TensorFlow process inside the native CPU kernel with an ASan-detected segmentation fault caused by a write memory access.

The crash occurs in:

```text
tensorflow::functor::HistogramFixedWidthFunctor<Eigen::ThreadPoolDevice, float, int>::Compute
```

Instead of rejecting the non-finite range or safely mapping the boundary values to the first/last histogram bins, TensorFlow enters the native histogram kernel and performs an invalid write.

```shell
print("tf:", tf.__version__)

    [
        [[inf, inf]],
        [[-inf, inf]],
        [[inf, inf]],
    ],
    dtype=tf.float32,
)

nbins = tf.constant(109, dtype=tf.int32)

print("values:")
print(values)
print("value_range:", value_range)
print("nbins:", nbins)

out = tf.histogram_fixed_width(
    values=values,
    value_range=value_range,
    nbins=nbins,
    dtype=tf.int32,
)

```

body:
[XLA:GPU] fix reshape contiguity check of partially tiled size-1 dims

We have wrongly assumed that it's completely safe to skip tile-size 1 dims, but for example we cannot tile [17,2,4] -> [136] with [4,1,4] tile sizes stride as tile [16].

I will follow up with more updates in tests.

title: Potential denial-of-service via unbounded allocation in tf.range / RangeOp
body:
### Issue type

Bug

### Have you reproduced the bug with TensorFlow Nightly?

Yes

### Source

source

### TensorFlow version

### Custom code

### OS platform and distribution

### Python version

### Bazel version

bazel-9.1.0

### GCC/compiler version

gcc (Ubuntu 11.4.0-1ubuntu1~22.04.2) 11.4.0

### CUDA/cuDNN version

_No response_

### GPU model and memory

_No response_

### Current behavior?

Calling `tf.range` with extreme floating-point arguments can make `RangeOp` infer a very large output length and attempt to allocate a multi-terabyte tensor. In my ASan-enabled build, this does not fail with a clean, catchable TensorFlow exception. Instead, the process aborts in the allocator with an `allocation-size-too-big` ASan report.

The reproducer below uses only three scalar Python inputs:

```text
start = -0.5
limit = 2.6623919835808085e+307
delta = 1.0162754537078317e+295
dtype = tf.float64
```

These values make `tf.range` infer approximately:

```text
ceil((limit - start) / delta) = 2619754293846 elements
```

Since the output dtype is `float64`, this results in an attempted allocation of:

```text
2619754293846 * 8 = 20958034350768 bytes
```

which is approximately 20.96 TB.

This can cause a denial-of-service condition when `tf.range` parameters are derived from untrusted or malformed user input. A small number of scalar inputs can force TensorFlow to attempt an extremely large allocation and abort the host process under ASan. Invalid or excessively large inferred output sizes should be rejected deterministically before allocation, preferably with a recoverable Python exception such as `ResourceExhaustedError` or `InvalidArgumentError`.

### Standalone code to reproduce the issue

```shell
import tensorflow as tf

def main():
    print("TensorFlow:", tf.__version__)

    start = -0.5
    limit = 2.6623919835808085e+307
    delta = 1.0162754537078317e+295
    dtype = tf.float64

    print("start =", start)
    print("limit =", limit)
    print("delta =", delta)
    print("dtype =", dtype)

    x = tf.range(
        start=start,
        limit=limit,
        delta=delta,
        dtype=dtype,
    )

    print(x)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

title: PR #45082: [XLA:GPU] Use packed storage shapes for FP4 XTile operands
body:
PR #45082: [XLA:GPU] Use packed storage shapes for FP4 XTile operands

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45082

📝 Summary of Changes
Update XTile codegen to model packed FP4 scaled-dot operands using their physical storage shape and storage element type. For packed f4E2M1FN operands, XTile now uses i8 storage, divides the packed layout-minor dimension by the number of FP4 elements per byte, adjusts tile offsets for the packed storage coordinate system, and validates that packed tiles use unit stride and byte-aligned offsets. This is the second PR in the decomposition of the larger scaled-dot fix series: https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44223.

🎯 Justification
FP4 scaled-dot operands are stored packed: two logical f4E2M1FN values live in one byte. After https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44885, XTile can carry the logical dot element type separately from the tensor storage type. This PR makes the tile and memref storage side consistent with that contract.

This cannot be delayed until Triton lowering because XTile already materializes memref types, tile shapes, slice offsets, and extract geometry before Triton sees the operation. If XTile keeps using logical FP4 shapes at that layer, it can describe incorrect byte storage shapes, tile sizes, and offsets for packed FP4 data. This matters for NVFP4/MXFP4 scaled-dot workloads lowered through Triton, where Triton expects e2m1 operands to be carried as packed i8 storage.

🚀 Kind of Contribution
🐛 Bug Fix, 🧪 Tests

🧪 Unit Tests:
TritonDevicelessTest.RejectsPackedFp4OddMinorOffset verifies that packed FP4 tiles reject byte-unaligned minor offsets.
TritonDevicelessTest.EmitsPackedFp4StorageForEvenMinorOffset verifies that byte-aligned packed FP4 operands use packed i8 memrefs/tensors, storage-coordinate offsets, and dot_scaled i8 storage element types.

title: PR #44992: [ROCm] Serialize rocm_smi access during parallel device init
body:
PR #44992: [ROCm] Serialize rocm_smi access during parallel device init

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/44992

XLA initializes devices concurrently (PlatformUtil::GetStreamExecutors), so GetRocmPcieBandwidth and GetRocmXgmiTopology issue rsmi_* calls in parallel. rocm_smi only guards state with a per-device mutex, but its gpu_metrics object is a process-global singleton, so concurrent queries on different devices corrupt its shared std::map and SEGV. Hold a global mutex across each rsmi call sequence.

title: Fix embedded buffer allocation in DynamicSliceFusionV2Thunk
body:
Fix embedded buffer allocation in DynamicSliceFusionV2Thunk

During thunk preparation and initialization, DynamicSliceFusionV2Thunk
previously forwarded the parent computation's buffer allocations to embedded
thunk executors. For embedded thunks (e.g., CustomCallThunk), allocation
indices refer to synthetic embedded allocations rather than parent
allocation indices, leading to out-of-bounds size checks when parent
allocation sizes differed from embedded allocation sizes.

This change updates DynamicSliceFusionV2Thunk::Prepare and Initialize to
build embedded buffer allocations and pass them to embedded thunk
executors.

title: [XLA:evaluator] Fix count-leading-zeros for negative signed integers

[XLA:evaluator] Fix count-leading-zeros for negative signed integers

The HLO evaluator sign extended narrow signed operands to 64 bits before
counting leading zeros, so e.g. clz of s32 0xC1A63AF0 evaluated to -32
instead of 0. Mask the operand to its own bit width before counting so the
result stays in [0, bitwidth] and matches the codegen backends (llvm.ctlz)
for all integer types.

title: Fix XLA DenseBincount negative input validation for runtime tensors
body:
## Summary

PR #121118 added compile-time constant validation for negative inputs in the XLA `DenseBincount` kernel. However, it only handles the case where the input is a **compile-time constant** (e.g., `tf.constant([0, -1, 2])`). For **runtime (non-constant) tensors** — the common case in `@tf.function(jit_compile=True)` where inputs come from placeholders, variables, or upstream ops — negative values are still passed directly to `xla::Scatter`, silently producing wrong results instead of raising `InvalidArgumentError` as eager mode does.

This PR fixes the runtime case that #121118 left unfixed.

### Approach

For runtime (non-constant) inputs, since XLA cannot raise runtime errors from within a compiled computation, we:

1. **Build a mask** `nonneg_mask = xla::Ge(input, 0)` — true where input >= 0
2. **Set negative indices to `output_size`** (out of bounds) via `xla::Select` so that XLA Scatter silently ignores them (verified: XLA Scatter drops out-of-bounds updates)

Using OOB indices instead of clamping to 0 avoids a subtle bug with `binary_output=True`: when scatter assigns (rather than adds), clamping negative values to index 0 would overwrite legitimate bin 0 values with 0. OOB indices are simply dropped by XLA Scatter, preserving correct results.

> **Note:** An earlier revision of this PR also zeroed the corresponding updates via `xla::Mul(updates, ConvertElementType(mask, dtype))` as a belt-and-suspenders measure. This was removed in commit `3560814` per review feedback — it is redundant because XLA Scatter already drops out-of-bounds updates, and zeroing could actually make a hypothetical backend OOB-clamping bug *worse* for `ScatterAssign` (assigning 0 over valid bin-0 data). The OOB-index approach alone is sufficient and safer.

### Compile-time constant inputs

The existing validation from #121118 is preserved unchanged — `OP_REQUIRES` raises `InvalidArgumentError` at compile time for constant negative inputs.

## Test plan

- [ ] `testNegativeInputRuntimeIgnored`: 1D runtime input with negatives → negative values ignored, correct counts for non-negative values
- [ ] `testNegativeInputRuntimeIgnoredBinary`: `binary_output=True` with runtime negatives → negative values ignored, no bin 0 overwrite
- [ ] `testNegativeInputRuntime2d`: 2D runtime input with negatives → per-row bincount correct, negatives ignored

```bash
python tensorflow/compiler/tests/bincount_op_test.py
```

Closes #117960

title: Declare `xla::ifrt::Value::Destroy` as virtual
body:
Declare `xla::ifrt::Value::Destroy` as virtual

`tsl::ReferenceCounted<T>` by default declares `Destroy` to be non-virtual in order to avoid introducing a vtable for `T` that doesn't need vtable otherwise. For `xla::ifrt::Value`, this prevents implementations from overriding the destroy behavior since `tsl::RCReference<ValueRef>` will always call `Value::Destroy()` even if implementations define their own destroy method.

This CL declares `Value::Destroy` as virtual so that implementations can override it if needed. Since `Value` already needs a vtable, this should introduce a minimal overhead.

title: Update the pinned `ruy` dependency — current pin (Sep 2022) predates upstream fixes for `ruy::CpuInfo::Initialize()` SIGSEGV on Android
body:
### Request

Please bump the pinned `ruy` commit in [`third_party/ruy/workspace.bzl`](https://github.com/tensorflow/tensorflow/blob/master/third_party/ruy/workspace.bzl). It is currently pinned to `google/ruy@3286a34cc8de6149ac6844107dfdffac91531e72` (**2022-09-14**), which is ~3.5 years old and predates several **already-merged upstream `ruy` fixes** for null-pointer crashes in CPU detection on Android.

### Problem

TFLite users hit a native crash in `ruy::CpuInfo::Initialize()` — a null-pointer dereference (SIGSEGV, fault address `0x8`) during CPU cache/topology detection — on a subset of Android devices (frequently Xiaomi/Vivo/Redmi) and in sandboxed processes. Representative symbolicated stack:

```
#00 ruy::CpuInfo::Initialize()          cpuinfo.cc:66
#02 ruy::CpuInfo::NeonDotprod()         cpuinfo.cc:35
#03 ruy::Ctx::GetRuntimeEnabledPaths()  ctx.cc:125
#04 ruy::Ctx::SelectPath(ruy::Path)     ctx.cc:177
```

This has been reported repeatedly — e.g. tensorflow/tensorflow#75815 (moved to google-ai-edge/LiteRT#36) and google/ruy#349 — and affects thousands of users in production.

### Root cause — fixes already merged upstream in `ruy`

The crash is fixed by commits that landed in `google/ruy` **after** the currently-pinned `3286a34c`:

- [`690c14c4`](https://github.com/google/ruy/commit/690c14c441387a4ea6e07a9ed89657cec8200b92) — "Ensure that processors are non-null before trying to get their cores" (adds null-guards for `processor_start`/`processor_end` in `QueryCacheParams`).
- [`c08ec529fc`](https://github.com/google/ruy/commit/c08ec529fc91722bde519628d9449258082eb847) — "Change QueryCacheParams to return if there was an error and handle that during Initialize". This converts debug-only `RUY_DCHECK_GT(...)` guards — which compile to **no-ops in `-c opt` builds** (how TFLite ships) — into real runtime checks that fall back to dummy cache params and return `kFailed`, instead of proceeding with invalid CPU state.
- [`32dd2b92`](https://github.com/google/ruy/commit/32dd2b9262caff9a8dc8d1436bc7f9d4ff2be26e) — "handle null cpuinfo_get_arch".
- `c04e5e52` — "Also check for null cpuinfo_uarch in CurrentCpuIsX1()".

Because the current pin predates all of these, the guards that would prevent the crash are compiled out in release TFLite builds, so it reaches production.

### Suggested fix

Bump `third_party/ruy/workspace.bzl` to a recent `google/ruy` commit that includes the above (current `ruy` HEAD is `2af888636`, 2026-02-17). This is a **pin bump only** — the fixes are already merged upstream; no `ruy` code changes are needed.

We have verified that rebuilding TFLite against a newer `ruy` containing these commits resolves the crash, with no other changes.

### System information

- Affects: TensorFlow Lite / LiteRT Android release builds, on all recent TF versions (the `ruy` pin is unchanged on `master`).
- Currently pinned `ruy`: `3286a34cc8de6149ac6844107dfdffac91531e72` (2022-09-14).

title: PR #45062: [XLA:GPU] Add VMM-persistent command buffer temp allocations
body:
PR #45062: [XLA:GPU] Add VMM-persistent command buffer temp allocations

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45062

Stacked on #44296. This PR should be reviewed and merged after #44296.

Currently, `NEVER_UPDATE` and `CAPTURE_CMD_NEVER_UPDATE` mode is to avoid graph update through VMM memory allocator's VA-remapping, but it seems that they are not not always work well for  all workloads. So  this PR want to clean the va-remap mode and make the va-remap mode more conservative (just introduce mode with confident speedup).

📝 Summary of Changes

- Define two command-buffer update modes: `ALWAYS_UPDATE` and `SKIP_TEMP`.
- Treat referenced constants as persistent in both modes.
- In `SKIP_TEMP`, give command-buffer-referenced preallocated temporary buffers stable VMM reservation addresses while parameters and live-out buffers remain dynamically updated.
- Collect the persistent and VA-remapped allocation indices once when `GpuExecutableBufferAllocator` is instantiated, and pass the resulting persistent vector directly to command-buffer execution.
- Remove the former address-policy mode state, redundant checks, dead accessors, and the intermediate allocation-index collection API.
- Document allocator selection, non-VMM fallback, and the resulting address policy.

🎯 Justification

Command buffers can avoid unnecessary address updates for executable-owned temporary buffers when those buffers retain stable virtual addresses. Restricting VMM remapping to preallocated temporaries preserves the caller's normal parameter and output allocation semantics. The simplified allocator state also makes the fallback and remapping behavior easier to follow and maintain.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature, ♻️ Cleanup

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

Not applicable; this PR changes allocation policy and correctness coverage rather than claiming a measured performance improvement.

🧪 Unit Tests:

- `bazel test //xla:debug_options_flags_test`
- `bazel test //xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_test`
- Added coverage for update-mode defaults and parsing, mixed constant/temp/parameter/live-out allocation policy, and non-VMM fallback behavior.

🧪 Execution Tests:

- Added repeated two-GEMM command-buffer coverage verifying that the intermediate temp uses one reusable VMM reservation.
- Added execution coverage for `SKIP_TEMP` fallback with a non-VMM allocator.

title: PR #45220: [HLO] Guard out-of-bounds dimension access in all-gather reshape match
body:
PR #45220: [HLO] Guard out-of-bounds dimension access in all-gather reshape match

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45220

### Problem
The `get_reshaped_all_gather_dimension` lambda in `GetAllGatherTransformations` (`collective_transformation_reorderer.cc`) can read one past the end of the shape's `DimensionVector`.

### Root cause
The loop (lines 87-93) advances `reshaped_all_gather_dimension` while it is `< rank` **and** `reshaped_num_strides < all_gather_num_strides`. When it exits because the index reached the rank *at the same moment* the stride counts became equal — which happens when the all-gather dimension and any trailing dims are size 1, so `product(dims[all_gather_dim:]) == 1` — the guard at line 94 (`reshaped_num_strides != all_gather_num_strides`) passes, and line 101 then evaluates `shape().dimensions(reshaped_all_gather_dimension)` with the index equal to the rank. `Shape::dimensions(int)` indexes the `DimensionVector` with no bounds check (fires `ABSL_HARDENING_ASSERT` under hardened builds, reads OOB otherwise).

Concrete trigger: all-gather output `[6, 1]`, `all_gather_dimension = 1`, single-user reshape to `[6]`.

### Fix
Return `nullopt` when the index reaches the rank, mirroring the loop's own bound.

### Verification
Static reasoning (loop/index math). No bazel build available on my machine; happy to add a test with a size-1 all-gather dimension followed by a reshape.

[HLO] Guard out-of-bounds dimension access in all-gather reshape match

get_reshaped_all_gather_dimension's loop can exit with the dimension
index equal to the shape rank when all reshape dimensions are consumed to
reach the stride count (e.g. a size-1 all-gather dimension). The stride
equality guard passes in that case and the following
shape().dimensions(reshaped_all_gather_dimension) read one past the end
of the DimensionVector. Return nullopt when the index reaches the rank,
mirroring the loop's own bound.

reshaped rank, leaving the candidate reshaped all-gather dimension equal to

the transformation is now rejected (no reorder).

title: PR #45219: [SPMD] Fix instruction-height recurrence in schedule-aware collective CSE
body:
PR #45219: [SPMD] Fix instruction-height recurrence in schedule-aware collective CSE

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45219

### Problem
`RunOnComputation` in `schedule_aware_collective_ops_cse.cc` computes instruction "height" (distance to root) incorrectly for any multi-user node, corrupting the heuristic that gates schedule-aware CSE.

### Root cause
```cpp
for (auto user : hlo->users()) {
  h = std::max(h, height[user]) + 1;   // +1 applied per user
}
```
The `+ 1` binds outside `std::max`, and `h` is reassigned each iteration, so a node with N users accumulates roughly `+N` instead of a single `+1` on top of the max child height (the result is also order-dependent). For example, two height-0 users yield height 2 where the true longest-path height is 1. This inflated height feeds `coll_height` and `lowest_user_height` into the CSE gate `lowest_user_height(earlier_coll) > coll_height + distance_threshold` (line 152).

### Fix
Move the `+1` inside the max (`std::max(h, height[user] + 1)`) — the canonical longest-path recurrence — matching the no-`+1` reads in `lowest_user_height`.

### Impact / verification
Scheduling/CSE quality heuristic (live-range / peak-memory), not a numerical miscompile. Static reasoning; trivially checkable (two zero-height users → 1, not 2).

Copybara import of the project:

--
a53f280d7032ea6085214a3fef9c22e3cfdf57f5 by Eylon Krause <eylon1909@gmail.com>:

[SPMD] Fix instruction-height recurrence in schedule-aware collective CSE

The height recurrence applied `+ 1` to the running max on every user
iteration (`h = std::max(h, height[user]) + 1;`), so a node's height was
inflated by roughly its user count instead of being
max_over_users(height[user]) + 1. That corrupts the height and
lowest_user_height values that gate the CSE schedule-distance heuristic.
Move the +1 inside the max (`std::max(h, height[user] + 1)`), the
canonical longest-path recurrence, matching the no-+1 reads in
lowest_user_height.

title: PR #45221: [SPMD] Read constant dynamic-update-slice start index via GetIntegralAsS64
body:
PR #45221: [SPMD] Read constant dynamic-update-slice start index via GetIntegralAsS64

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45221

### Problem
`AnalyzeDynamicUpdateSlice` (`spmd_partitioner_util.cc`) reads a constant dynamic-update-slice start index with a type that is only correct for S32/S64, so a valid integral index of another type is mis-read.

### Root cause
```cpp
int64_t start_index =
    elemType == S64 ? hlo->operand(i + 2)->literal().Get<int64_t>({})
                    : hlo->operand(i + 2)->literal().Get<int>({});
```
`Get<int>` requires the literal's element type to be S32, so for a `U32`/`U64`/`S16`/... index it trips the literal's element-type check (and under `NDEBUG` silently reinterprets the underlying buffer). `ShapeInference::InferDynamicUpdateSliceShape` permits any integral index type, so such indices are valid HLO. The sibling constant-index read a few lines below (line ~3576) already uses the type-agnostic `GetIntegralAsS64`.

### Fix
Use `GetIntegralAsS64({})`, matching that sibling.

### Impact / verification
Latent robustness bug (mainline frontends emit S32/S64). Static reasoning. Happy to add a test with a `U32`-typed DUS index.

title: check output buffer size in SnappyInputBuffer::Inflate
body:
1. Inflate reads the uncompressed block length from the (untrusted) snappy stream and only validates it against output_buffer_capacity_ with DCHECK_GE, which is compiled out in release builds.
2. Snappy_Uncompress then writes uncompressed_length bytes into the fixed output_buffer_, so a block declaring a length larger than the buffer overflows the heap. This is reachable from tf.data CustomReader, which reads snapshot files with a 32 MiB output buffer.

Replaced the DCHECK with the runtime ResourceExhausted check that SnappyInputStream already uses, and added the matching SmallUncompressOutputBuffer test.

title: PR #45255: [XLA:GPU] Keep VMM mappings alive across executions in command buffer va-remapping run.
body:
PR #45255: [XLA:GPU] Keep VMM mappings alive across executions in command buffer va-remapping run.

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45255

## What

Removes the blanket `SynchronizePendingOperations()` drain from `GpuExecutableBufferAllocator::CreateExecutionScope`, so in the command buffer run with va-remapping, deferred deallocations and unmaps from the previous execution stay pending and the next execution reactivates the compatible stale mappings at the same reservation VAs.

## Why

The drain completed every deferred operation before each execution:

* the host spin-waited until the previous execution's teardown seqno retired on the GPU, blocking host run-ahead every step, and
* the reservation-VA mappings were torn down and their physical allocations released, so every step paid fresh physical allocations plus remapping work for each VA-remapped allocation, and the physical handle behind the stable VA changed on every step.

The allocator already handles the leftover state correctly, so the drain is unnecessary:

* `Allocate()` reactivates a compatible stale mapping at the same reservation VA (`TryReuseMappedAllocationAtReservationAddress`, `TryReuseMappedAllocationWithSeparateAddress`), and `Map()` reactivates a stale alias for the same raw allocation and range, keeping the same physical allocation across executions with no unmap/remap work,
* incompatible stale mappings are completed lazily and per-record by the fresh-mapping paths (`EnsureReservationAvailableForFreshMapping` and the `Map()` target preparation), and
* memory pressure is handled by the `ResourceExhausted` reclaim path.

The destructor still synchronizes pending operations so the module-owned VA reservation outlives any stale mappings into it.

With this change, in steady state the VA→physical mapping for VA-remapped allocations is never torn down between executions, which also keeps physical-handle-caching consumers (e.g. `CollectiveMemoryCache` registrations keyed by VA) consistent with the addresses command buffers capture.

## Tests

New tests in `cuda_device_address_vmm_allocator_test.cc`:

* `BackToBackMappedAllocationsReuseMappingsAcrossSteps` — simulates consecutive executable runs over a shared two-slice reservation layout: each step allocates the same slices, runs stream work through the reservation addresses, and defers deallocation at teardown with no synchronization between steps. Asserts later steps reactivate the same physical allocation and verifies stream-ordered data flow through mappings that are never torn down.
* `AllocateIntoReservationRejectsSizeChangeAtSameAddress` — pins that a different-size request at the same reservation offset is rejected as a partial overlap instead of remapping underneath the pending teardown, and that the stale mapping stays reusable for a matching request.

title: Add experimental GDS filesystem plugin scaffold with read_to_device support
body:
This change adds an experimental TensorFlow filesystem plugin for the `gds` URI scheme, intended for NVIDIA GPUDirect Storage use cases.

It includes:
- a new GDS filesystem implementation under `tensorflow/c/experimental/filesystem/plugins/gds/`
- `read_to_device` support on `TF_RandomAccessFileOps` for direct-to-device reads
- a build target for the plugin
- a version bump in filesystem_interface.h to match the new optional API field

The implementation is intentionally scoped as a scaffold:
- host reads still work through the standard `read` path
- direct GPU reads return `TF_UNIMPLEMENTED` when GDS is unavailable, so callers can fall back cleanly
- the plugin target is Linux-only and marked manual/non-default

title: Fix XLA nonnegative inference for signed integers
body:
Fixes #118178.

This fixes an incorrect `AlgebraicSimplifier::IsNonNegative` inference for signed integer HLO. Signed integer `x * x` and `abs(x)` are not guaranteed to be non-negative because overflow can produce or preserve a negative value, as in the `s8` case from the issue.

The change keeps the simplifier conservative for signed integer `multiply(x, x)` and `abs(x)`, and adds regression coverage for the `s8` `compare` / `abs` / `select` pattern.

Validation:
- `git diff --check`
- Not run: `bazel test //xla/hlo/transforms/simplifiers:algebraic_simplifier_test --test_filter='*SignedInteger*:*DoesNotFoldSignedIntegerSquareAbsSelect*'` because `bazel` / `bazelisk` is not installed in this local environment.

title: PR #45062: [XLA:GPU] Add VMM-persistent command buffer temp allocations
body:
PR #45062: [XLA:GPU] Add VMM-persistent command buffer temp allocations

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45062

Stacked on #44296. This PR should be reviewed and merged after #44296.

Currently, `NEVER_UPDATE` and `CAPTURE_CMD_NEVER_UPDATE` mode is to avoid graph update through VMM memory allocator's VA-remapping, but it seems that they are not not always work well for  all workloads. So  this PR want to clean the va-remap mode and make the va-remap mode more conservative (just introduce mode with confident speedup) by only allowing va-remapping for TEMP buffer.

📝 Summary of Changes

- Define two command-buffer update modes: `ALWAYS_UPDATE` and `SKIP_TEMP`.
- Treat referenced constants as persistent in both modes.
- In `SKIP_TEMP`, give command-buffer-referenced preallocated temporary buffers stable VMM reservation addresses while parameters and live-out buffers remain dynamically updated.
- Collect the persistent and VA-remapped allocation indices once when `GpuExecutableBufferAllocator` is instantiated, and pass the resulting persistent vector directly to command-buffer execution.
- Remove the former address-policy mode state, redundant checks, dead accessors, and the intermediate allocation-index collection API.
- Document allocator selection, non-VMM fallback, and the resulting address policy.

🎯 Justification

Command buffers can avoid unnecessary address updates for executable-owned temporary buffers when those buffers retain stable virtual addresses. Restricting VMM remapping to preallocated temporaries preserves the caller's normal parameter and output allocation semantics. The simplified allocator state also makes the fallback and remapping behavior easier to follow and maintain.

🚀 Kind of Contribution

✨ New Feature, ♻️ Cleanup

📊 Benchmark (for Performance Improvements)

Not applicable; this PR changes allocation policy and correctness coverage rather than claiming a measured performance improvement.

🧪 Unit Tests:

- `bazel test //xla:debug_options_flags_test`
- `bazel test //xla/service/gpu:gpu_executable_test`
- Added coverage for update-mode defaults and parsing, mixed constant/temp/parameter/live-out allocation policy, and non-VMM fallback behavior.

🧪 Execution Tests:

- Added repeated two-GEMM command-buffer coverage verifying that the intermediate temp uses one reusable VMM reservation.
- Added execution coverage for `SKIP_TEMP` fallback with a non-VMM allocator.

- the plugin target is Linux-only and marked manual/non-default

title: Fix avgpool3dgrad crash

labels.name: comp:core
labels.description: issues related to core part of tensorflow

body:
Fixes #118354

### Description
This PR fixes a fatal `CHECK` failure in the `AvgPool3DGrad` C++ API kernel that occurs when invalid input shapes or gradients are provided.

Previously, `MklAvgPoolingGradOp::Compute` lacked validation for the rank of the gradient and input shape tensors before converting them to oneDNN formats (via `TFShapeToMklDnnDimsInNCDHW`). If a malformed tensor (such as a 0-rank scalar) was passed, the process would abort/core dump because the underlying utility expected at least a 4D or 5D shape.

### Changes Made
- Added rank and element count validation for `orig_input_tensor` inside `tensorflow/core/kernels/mkl/mkl_avgpooling_op.cc`
- Added rank validation for `grad_tensor` based on whether the op is configured for 2D or 3D pooling.
- Instead of terminating the host process, the kernel now gracefully returns an `absl::InvalidArgumentError` when an invalid shape is detected, matching the expected behavior of native TensorFlow kernels.

### Motivation and Context
Prevents malicious or accidental malformed graphs from crashing the host process, particularly important for runtime stability and security in distributed or production environments.

### Type of change
- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

title: Fix false shape-mismatch in XLA Igamma/Igammac/Zeta for operands with identical logical shape
body:
Fixes issue #122047.

**Description**
The shape equality check in XLA operations `Igamma`, `IgammaGradA`, `RandomGammaGrad`, `Igammac`, and `Zeta` was previously using `operator!=` (`Shape::Equal()`). This strict equality check inappropriately compares dynamic-dimension bits and layouts in addition to logical dimensions and element types. 

When one operand originates from a path that propagates a dynamic-dimension bit (e.g. `tf.linalg.lstsq`) while the other operand does not (e.g., `tf.experimental.numpy.power`), the two `xla::Shape` objects compare as unequal. This triggers a failure even though their printed representation and logical semantics are identical. The check would confusingly fire with: `"must have equal shapes and types; got f64[6,32,32] and f64[6,32,32]"`.

**The Fix**
Replaced `operator!=` with `!ShapeUtil::Compatible()`, which is defined as `Shape::Equal().IgnoreDynamicDimension().IgnoreLayout()`. This safely accepts any pair of shapes that share the same rank, bounded dimensions, and element type, correctly validating the op constraints without falsely failing on dynamic dimension metadata.

**Testing**
- Added C++ unit tests in `math_test.cc` (`IgammaDynamicShapeMismatch`, `IgammacDynamicShapeMismatch`, and `ZetaDynamicShapeMismatch`) that verify the build succeeds when one operand carries a dynamic-dimension bit and the other does not.
- Added a Python regression test `DynamicShapeEqualityTest` in `special_math_test.py` that reliably reproduces the original failure chain (`logaddexp -> linspace -> lstsq/power -> Igamma/Igammac/Zeta`) under `jit_compile=True` and asserts that the eager execution outputs match the XLA execution outputs.

Existing shape-validation tests are unaffected; genuine rank or element-type mismatches still cleanly return `InvalidArgument`.

title: Add Tan opcode support to XLA constant/dynamism value inference
body:
Fix #122050.

When tf.math.tan output feeds an op that XLA's constant-value analysis must evaluate at compile time (e.g., the limit input to Range, via tf.sequence_mask), jit_compile=True compilation failed with:

  InvalidArgumentError: AnalyzeConstantValueFallback can't handle opcode: tan

Root cause: kTan was absent from the AnalyzeConstant switch in xla/hlo/builder/value_inference.cc. The function has an explicit case block for kSin and kCos that routes through HloProtoEvaluator; kTan should have been included there but was not. The omission caused AnalyzeConstant to fall through to its default branch, which calls AnalyzeConstantValueFallback. That fallback explicitly lists kTan in its error-return case (correct for upper/lower-bound analysis where transcendentals have no useful bound), producing the observed error.

Fix: add kTan to the AnalyzeConstant evaluator switch alongside kSin and kCos. HloProtoEvaluator already supports kTan (eager execution works), so no new evaluation logic is required.

Note: AnalyzeIsDynamic already handles kTan correctly. No change to AnalyzeConstantValueFallback or AnalyzeIsDynamic is needed.

title: TorchTpu drops dead nodes: if a collective's result is unused on the
body:
TorchTpu drops dead nodes: if a collective's result is unused on the
local rank, that rank's program skips it. Collectives require
participation from every rank in the group, so the drop makes the
remaining ranks hang.

This commit marks every dispatched collective as keep-alive, so the
traversal retains and emits it even when no output depends on it.

title: Fix tf.experimental.numpy.isclose XLA shape mismatch
body:
Fixes #122052.

This change makes the non-inexact path of `tf.experimental.numpy.isclose` use strict TensorFlow equality for non-broadcastable inputs.

Tensor equality normally returns scalar `False` for incompatible shapes through the incompatible-shape fallback. Under `jit_compile=True`, the graph could still contain an `Equal` operation over incompatible shapes, causing XLA compilation to fail.

The non-inexact path now uses `math_ops.equal`, which applies strict broadcasting rules. As a result, non broadcastable inputs raise a `ValueError` or TensorFlow equivalent instead of returning `False` in eager execution and failing later during XLA compilation. This also keeps the behavior consistent with NumPy and with the existing inexact-type path.

The change is placed in `isclose` so that both direct `isclose` calls and `allclose`, which reduces the result of `isclose`, receive the fix.

The regression test covers both `isclose` and `allclose` with integer and floating-point inputs in eager and XLA-compiled execution.

## Testing

```bash
bazel test --config=linux -k \
  //tensorflow/python/ops/numpy_ops:np_math_ops_test \
  --test_filter='*CloseNonBroadcastableShapesXla*'

bazel test --config=linux -k \
  //tensorflow/python/ops/numpy_ops:np_math_ops_test
```

title: tf.lite.TFLiteConverter.convert() leaks memory on every call; not released after converter deletion + gc (2.20 / 2.21 / nightly)
body:
### Issue type

Bug (memory leak / performance)

### Have you reproduced the bug with TensorFlow Nightly?

Yes — reproduced on `tf-nightly==2.22.0.dev20260702`, on `2.21.0` (latest
stable), and on `2.20.0`.

### Source

binary (pip)

### TensorFlow version

2.21.0 (latest stable); also reproduced on 2.22.0-dev20260702 (nightly) and 2.20.0

### Custom code

Yes

### OS platform and distribution

Linux x86_64

### Python version

3.13 (CPython)

### GPU model and memory

CPU only (`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1`)

### Current behavior?

`tf.lite.TFLiteConverter.convert()` retains process memory on **every** call.
The memory is **not** released when the converter object is deleted and
`gc.collect()` runs, so RSS grows ~linearly with the number of conversions in a
single process. The leaked amount scales with model complexity (negligible for a
tiny MLP; **~20 MB per `convert()` for DenseNet121**).

I isolated the leak to the `convert()` step (SavedModel → MLIR → TFLite
flatbuffer). Each loop below repeats over the **same** artifact with
`del` + `gc.collect()` between iterations; RSS measured with `psutil`:

| Loop | RSS slope | |
|---|---|---|
| `TFLiteConverter.from_saved_model()` (load only, no convert) | ~0 MB/iter | flat |
| **`converter.convert()`** | **+12 … +20 MB/iter** | **leaks** |
| `ai_edge_litert` `Interpreter` load + `allocate_tensors` + `invoke` | +0.00 MB/iter (25 iters) | flat |

So it is not SavedModel loading and not inference — only `.convert()`. It also
reproduces with a hand-built raw `tf.Module` deep conv net (no keras at all),
though the per-call amount there is small and close to the RSS noise floor;
DenseNet121 gives a large, unambiguous signal. `keras.backend.clear_session()`
does not reclaim it; a Linux `malloc_trim(0)` reclaims only ~40% — indicating
native allocations retained inside the converter/MLIR pipeline.

**Reproduced on every version tested** (DenseNet121, N iterations, RSS via psutil):

| TF version | `convert()` behavior |
|---|---|
| 2.20.0 (release) | +20 MB/iter, clean monotonic growth |
| 2.21.0 (latest stable) | +22 MB/iter, clean monotonic growth |
| 2.22.0-dev20260702 (nightly) | noisier per-call, but the RSS **floor** (min retained) rises +100…+160 MB over 18–25 iters (least-squares +10…+13 MB/iter) |

On nightly the per-call transient allocation swings are larger, so the RSS floor
(minimum retained memory across iterations) is the reliable indicator — it
climbs steadily, i.e. the leak persists.

**Impact.** Any process that converts many models sequentially grows unbounded:
batch conversion, export services, notebooks, and CI. Concretely it OOM-kills a
16 GB GitHub-hosted runner when a test suite converts ~130 models in one process
(via `keras.Model.export(format="litert")`), even though each conversion
individually succeeds.

### Standalone code to reproduce the issue

```python
import gc, os, sys, tempfile
os.environ.setdefault("CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES", "-1")
os.environ.setdefault("TF_CPP_MIN_LOG_LEVEL", "2")
import psutil, tensorflow as tf

P = psutil.Process()
rss = lambda: P.memory_info().rss / 1e6

def make_converter(sm):
    c = tf.lite.TFLiteConverter.from_saved_model(sm)
    c.target_spec.supported_ops = [
        tf.lite.OpsSet.TFLITE_BUILTINS, tf.lite.OpsSet.SELECT_TF_OPS]
    c.experimental_enable_resource_variables = True
    return c

def measure(label, fn, N):
    rows = []
    for i in range(N):
        fn(); gc.collect(); rows.append(rss())
        print(f"  [{label}] iter {i:2d} RSS={rows[-1]:8.1f} MB")
    t = rows[2:]
    slope = (t[-1] - t[0]) / (len(t) - 1)
    print(f"  ==> {label}: slope={slope:+.2f} MB/iter\n")

N = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 12
# DenseNet121 is used only as a source of a realistically-complex model.
model = tf.keras.applications.DenseNet121(
    weights=None, input_shape=(64, 64, 3), classes=10)
sm = tempfile.mkdtemp()
model.export(sm)          # -> TF SavedModel
del model; gc.collect()

print("A. converter.convert()          (expected: LEAK)")
measure("convert", lambda: make_converter(sm).convert(), N)
print("B. from_saved_model only, no convert  (expected: flat)")
measure("load", lambda: make_converter(sm), N)
```

Run: `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=-1 python repro.py 12`

### Relevant log output

```shell
tensorflow 2.21.0  N=12       # latest stable; full unedited curve

A. converter.convert()          (expected: LEAK)
  [convert] iter  0 RSS=  1089.0 MB
  [convert] iter  1 RSS=  1117.9 MB
  [convert] iter  2 RSS=  1174.1 MB
  [convert] iter  3 RSS=  1164.1 MB
  [convert] iter  4 RSS=  1222.0 MB
  [convert] iter  5 RSS=  1226.6 MB
  [convert] iter  6 RSS=  1260.5 MB
  [convert] iter  7 RSS=  1042.3 MB
  [convert] iter  8 RSS=  1345.2 MB
  [convert] iter  9 RSS=  1364.2 MB
  [convert] iter 10 RSS=  1339.3 MB
  [convert] iter 11 RSS=  1372.6 MB
  ==> convert: slope=+22.05 MB/iter   (growth +198.5 MB over iters 2..11)

B. from_saved_model only, no convert  (expected: flat)
  [load] iter  0 RSS=  1094.5 MB
  [load] iter  4 RSS=  1128.3 MB
  [load] iter  8 RSS=  1191.2 MB
  [load] iter 11 RSS=  1128.4 MB
  ==> load: slope=+0.75 MB/iter   (flat — bounded jitter, no accumulation)
```

Expected: the memory used by a `convert()` call should be released (or
bounded/reused across calls) after the converter is deleted and
garbage-collected, so that converting N models sequentially in one process has
bounded peak RSS.

title: Fix XLA DynamicStitch with missing indices
body:
## Summary

Fixes #122053.

This PR updates the XLA `DynamicStitch` implementation to match eager CPU/GPU behavior when indices are non-contiguous.

Previously, the XLA path required every output index from `0..max(indices)` to be present and failed with:

```text
InvalidArgumentError: not all indices are used
```

However, TensorFlow `DynamicStitch` semantics define the output shape as `[max(indices) + 1] + constant`, and the normal kernels allocate the full output, zero-fill it, and then copy indexed slices. This means missing output positions should be zero-filled rather than rejected.

## Changes

- Removed the XLA-only requirement that all output indices from `0..max(indices)` must be used.
- Emits zero slices for missing output positions in the XLA path.
- Preserves duplicate-index last-wins behavior.
- Adds a regression test covering missing indices and duplicate indices.

## Testing

```bash
bazelisk test --config=macos_arm64 -k //tensorflow/compiler/tests:dynamic_stitch_test \
  --test_filter='*DynamicStitchTest.testMissingIndicesZeroFilled*'

bazelisk test --config=macos_arm64 -k //tensorflow/compiler/tests:dynamic_stitch_test
```

Both passed locally on macOS arm64.

## Style checks

```bash
clang-format tensorflow/compiler/tf2xla/kernels/dynamic_stitch_op.cc --style=google > /tmp/dynamic_stitch_op.cc
diff tensorflow/compiler/tf2xla/kernels/dynamic_stitch_op.cc /tmp/dynamic_stitch_op.cc

PYLINTHOME=/tmp/pylint-cache pylint --rcfile=tensorflow/tools/ci_build/pylintrc tensorflow/compiler/tests/dynamic_stitch_test.py
```

`clang-format` produced no diff after formatting. `pylint` rated the touched Python test file 10.00/10; the local pylint version emitted rcfile compatibility warnings for TensorFlow's existing pylintrc.

title: tf2xla: fix Round op crashing on integer input under jit_compile=True
body:
Fixes #122048

## Problem
`tf.math.round` / `tf.raw_ops.Round` on integer tensors compiles fine in eager mode but crashes under `jit_compile=True` with:
```
Operands to RoundToEven must be real-valued floating-point, but got S32
```

## Root cause
The XLA kernel for `Round` unconditionally called `xla::RoundToEven(x)`, which XLA rejects for non-float types.

## Fix
Replace the `XLAJIT_MAKE_UNARY` one-liner with a custom `RoundOp` that checks `DataTypeIsInteger(ctx->input_type(0))`:
- Integer input → identity (no-op, mathematically correct)
- Float input → `xla::RoundToEven(x)` as before

title: Add MLIR verifier and support checks for XTile scaled dot
body:
Add MLIR verifier and support checks for XTile scaled dot

Enforce scale and operand element type constraints in the XTile dot_scaled
operation verifier and restrict Triton scaled dot support to valid 8-bit scale
types.
Specifically:
- Add a verifier to xtile.dot_scaled in MLIR to restrict scale element types
  to 8-bit scale types (f8e8m0fnu, f8e4m3fn, f8e5m2, i8/s8) and operand element
  types to supported float or int8/int4 types.
- Restrict IsTritonSupportedScaledDot in support.cc to allow only valid 8 bit
  scale tensors.
- Update dot_algorithms.cc to only bitcast scale tensors to i8 when the scale
  is Float8E8M0FNU (preserving native float8 scale types like f8e4m3fn and
  f8e5m2). When emulating ScaledDot on Hopper (no hardware support), they need
  to still have their original type.
- Add device and support tests for E4M3, E5M2 and EM8M0 scale types.

title: Support tf.bitcast on complex tensors under XLA
body:
Fixes #122051

### Problem

`tf.bitcast` with a complex source raises `UnimplementedError: Complex types not supported.` under `jit_compile=True`, while it succeeds in eager execution:

```python
@tf.function(jit_compile=True)
def f(x):
    return tf.bitcast(x, tf.int32)

f(tf.complex(tf.random.normal([4]), tf.random.normal([4])))  # crash
```

The failure reproduces identically on CPU and GPU and across TF 2.20/2.21, i.e. it is in the shared TF→XLA lowering path, not a backend.

### Root cause

`BitcastOp::Compile` in `tf2xla/kernels/cast_op.cc` rejected any complex source/destination outright. This mirrors a real limitation one layer down: `ShapeInference::InferBitcastConvertShape` returns `InvalidArgument("Conversion between complex and real type ...")` whenever exactly one side is complex, so `xla::BitcastConvertType` has no semantics for crossing the complex↔real boundary.

### Fix

Since a complex tensor is stored as contiguous `[real, imag]`, a complex→integer bitcast can be expressed with primitives XLA already supports: split into `Real`/`Imag`, lay them out as a trailing `[real, imag]` dimension, bitcast the real component type to the destination integer, then reshape to the shape the eager `Bitcast` kernel produces. No change to HLO is required.

This is scoped to the reported case (complex source → integer destination). Real→complex and complex→complex bitcasts continue to return the existing `UnimplementedError`.

### Validation

The op-level decomposition was checked to be **byte-for-byte identical to eager** `tf.bitcast` across `complex64/complex128 → int16/int32` (and the reverse round-trip), including adversarial bit patterns (`+inf`, NaN, denormal, `-0.0`, all-ones), and it compiles under `jit_compile=True`. A regression test covering the crashing cases is added in `cast_ops_test.py`.

> Note: I was unable to build TensorFlow from source locally, so the C++ has not been compiled on my machine — I'm relying on CI to build and run the tests. Happy to adjust based on CI results and review.

title: PR #45121: [tsl] Fix FileSystem::Extension for paths with a directory component
body:
PR #45121: [tsl] Fix FileSystem::Extension for paths with a directory component

Imported from GitHub PR https://github.com/openxla/xla/pull/45121

### Problem

`FileSystem::Extension` (`xla/tsl/platform/file_system.cc`) is meant to return the characters after the final `.` in a path's basename. It computes `pos` as the offset of the last `.` **within `basename`**, but then constructs the returned `string_view` from the **full `path`**:

```cpp
absl::string_view basename = this->Basename(path);
size_t pos = basename.rfind('.');
...
return absl::string_view(path.data() + pos + 1, path.size() - (pos + 1));  // uses path, not basename
```

`basename` is a later substring of `path` whenever `path` has a directory component, so applying the basename-relative `pos` to `path` indexes into the wrong location:

```
Extension("dir/file.txt")      -> "ile.txt"    (expected "txt")
Extension("a/b/c/name.tar.gz") -> "e.tar.gz"   (expected "gz")
Extension("/tmp/foo.log")      -> "/foo.log"   (expected "log")
Extension("file.txt")          -> "txt"        (correct — no directory)
Extension("noext")             -> ""           (correct)
```

The result is correct only in the `basename == path` case (no directory component).

### Fix

Build the returned view from `basename`, which is where `pos` was computed:

```cpp
return absl::string_view(basename.data() + pos + 1,
                         basename.size() - (pos + 1));
```

### Tests

Added `RamFileSystemTest.ExtensionUsesBasenameForPathsWithDirectory` to `xla/tsl/platform/ram_file_system_test.cc` (using `RamFileSystem` to exercise the inherited `FileSystem::Extension`). It covers directory-prefixed paths, an absolute path, a no-directory path, and a no-extension path; it fails on the current code and passes with the fix. There was previously no test covering `FileSystem::Extension`, which is how this survived.

Copybara import of the project:
